text.p: Knight-Ridder Inc said Thursday it expects an earnings increase of at least 20 percent for 1997, despite dilution from the acquisition of four newspapers from Walt Disney Co.
"We continue to anticipate an earnings increase for the year, despite dilution from the Disney acquisition, of at least 20 percent," Chief Financial Officer Ross Jones said.

The company, reporting higher second quarter results, said earnings rose on solid fundamentals in the newspaper industry. It earned $0.61 a share from continuing operations, up from $0.42 in the same quarter in 1996.
"It was a great quarter for newspapers," said Jones.
For the quarter, total advertising revenue, excluding the Disney group, was up eight percent, with particular strength in classified, but with retail and general both up as well, Knight-Ridder said.
Newsprint expense fell 28.9 percent and ad revenue in each of the company's large markets was up versus a year ago.
"We continue to expect the price of newsprint to remain constant until the end of this year or the early part of next year, despite two recent announcements of proposed price increases," said Jones.

"Should there be an increase at either of those times, we will not feel the impact until 1998 -- leaving us confident that the cost of newsprint will be about 15 percent less this year than last," he said.

Excluding the results from the Disney papers, classified advertising was up 11.7 percent for the second quarter, with help wanted up 20.6 percent. All of the 12 largest markets showed classified increases.

General advertising was up 8.7 percent, with virtually all of the strength concentrated in Philadelphia, San Jose and Detroit. Airlines, telecommunications and computers were strong in each of those markets.
Operating costs (excluding Disney) decreased 0.4 percent, due primarily to the newsprint, ink and supplements decline of 25.4 percent versus the same period a year ago.
Knight-Ridder publishes 35 daily newspapers in the United States with a readership of 9.5 million daily and 13.6 million on Sunday. It has 35 Web sites.
